findings.consequence: An incompatible target and impossible lifecycle facts can be labeled semantically conformant. Existing owning helpers still perform their own structural, lifecycle and authority checks, so this observation does not demonstrate an unauthorized mutation. It leaves the required typed semantic action contract and its negative acceptance unproven.
findings.observation: The delivered SHACL shape constrains only family, operation, request/target digest and text-valued target/status fields. It does not constrain target identity/type, permitted target paths, current/next state, positive target revision, or a resolved required capability. The evaluator copies targetType and requiredCapability from the matched contract; all contracts name generic core Capability. The current family matrix injects an impossible additional shape for each semantic-invalid case, so it proves that a SHACL failure blocks dispatch but not that the delivered action model rejects a semantically invalid request.
